body: Not really a bug, but a missing feature. Currently, node picking only works in the root viewport.

Ran into this since I have a similar setup that I've been using for my game.

Design-wise, it looks like you'd have to go to the `scene_debugger.cpp` file and update the 4 `_find_[canvas/3d]_item[s]_at_[pos/rect]` methods that begin [here](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/34f005d810e8967ee0d57afb78f8e0a64f473094/scene/debugger/scene_debugger.cpp#L2304) so that they each do additional nested raycasts when the collided-with item is a `SubviewportContainer` OR when the material of the collided-with item has a `ViewportTexture`. Or maybe it only reacts to `ViewportTexture` instances when they are assigned to a dedicated texture property on the item (like `Sprite3D`)? In which case, it would need to have a dedicated list of types and their properties that it checks against for a `ViewportTexture` match.

The complexity explodes if you try to account for any UV-mapped `ViewportTexture` that appears within any material through a shader. You'd have to somehow have the shader tell the Godot Editor where the coordinates of the `ViewportTexture` are so that it can map them to world space and check if the raycast collided with it. WAY too complicated for my bad-math brain. 😅 That all may not be worth it anyway for such a niche feature.

The main use case of a `SubviewportContainer` seems simple enough. assuming I understand the requirements correctly. I'm still relatively new to 3D dev though, so there's probably stuff I'm not considering.
